Do there exist an entire function F on C^n and a continuous function L: C^n → R_+ such that (1) for some r_1 > r_0 and some P > 0, every z outside G_{r_1}^b(F) satisfies (1/|F(z)|)|∂F(z)/∂b| ≤ P L(z), while (2) for every r_2 < r_0 one has sup_{z∈C^n \ G_{r_2}^b(F)} |∂F(z)/∂b|/(|F(z)|L(z)) = +∞ and n(r_2) ∈ (0,+∞)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $b \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$ be a fixed direction, let $F: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be an entire function (not identically zero), and let $L: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}_+$ be a positive continuous function. For $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$ consider the slice function $g_z(t) = F(z + tb)$, $t \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $n_z(\rho)$ denote the number of zeros of $g_z$ in the disc $\{t \in \mathbb{C} : |t| < \rho\}$ (counted with multiplicities), assuming $g_z \not\equiv 0$. Define
$$n(r) \;=\; \sup_{z \in \mathbb{C}^n} n_z\!\left(\frac{r}{L(z)}\right), \qquad r > 0,$$
and the "exceptional set"
$$G^b_r(F) \;=\; \bigcup_{w \in \mathbb{C}^n : F(w)=0} \Big\{ w + tb : |t| < \tfrac{r}{L(w)} \Big\}.$$
Let $\partial F(z)/\partial b$ denote the directional derivative of $F$ along $b$, and let $\lambda_b(r)$ be the directional regularity quantity
$$\lambda_b(r) \;=\; \sup\!\left\{ \frac{L(z_1)}{L(z_2)} \,:\, z_1 = z_2 + tb,\ |t| \le \frac{r}{\min\{L(z_1),L(z_2)\}} \right\}.$$
Set
$$r_0 \;=\; \sup_{r>0} \frac{r}{2\, n(r)\, \lambda_b(r)}.$$

Question: Do there exist an entire function $F$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and a positive continuous function $L: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}_+$ such that both of the following hold?
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exist $r_1 > r_0$ and $P > 0$ such that
$$\frac{1}{|F(z)|}\left|\frac{\partial F(z)}{\partial b}\right| \;\le\; P\, L(z) \qquad \text{for every } z \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus G^b_{r_1}(F).$$
\item For every $r_2 < r_0$,
$$\sup_{z \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus G^b_{r_2}(F)} \frac{1}{|F(z)|\, L(z)} \left|\frac{\partial F(z)}{\partial b}\right| \;=\; +\infty,$$
and $n(r_2) \in (0, +\infty)$.
\end{enumerate}
In other words, is the threshold $r_0$ sharp in the sense that an entire function exhibiting this exact transition between bounded and unbounded normalized directional logarithmic derivative on the complement of the tube $G^b_r(F)$ actually exists?
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns sharpness of the threshold $r_0$ in the directional logarithmic-derivative criterion for entire functions of bounded L-index in direction. Surveys and follow-up papers by Bandura, Skaskiv and collaborators (2017–2020) have established sufficient conditions and sharper estimates of this type, but no source located definitively settles the existence of an extremal pair $(F,L)$ realizing the exact transition at $r_0$ described in the problem. The status appears to remain open or at least not publicly resolved.

status_evidence.title: Directional Logarithmic Derivative and the Distribution of Zeros of an Entire Function of Bounded L-Index Along the Direction
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes criteria for boundedness of L-index along a direction in terms of directional logarithmic derivative and zero distribution.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related criteria are established but the sharpness/extremal-example problem at $r_0$ is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Entire Functions of Bounded L-Index: Its Zeros and Behavior of Partial Logarithmic Derivatives
status_evidence.snippet: Provides multidimensional sufficient conditions for boundedness of L-index in joint variables involving partial logarithmic derivatives outside exceptional sets.
status_evidence.claim: Provides sufficient conditions but does not exhibit an entire function realizing the sharp threshold $r_0$ as in the posed problem.
